channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyz Interior Minister Awarded Order of Manas First Degree
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Interior Minister Ulan Niyazbekov has been awarded the Order of Manas First Degree. The award, decided long before the professional holiday, coincides with the Day of Kyrgyz Militia. This state recognition highlights the minister's significant influence beyond media presence.

item.title: IFJ Urges Prosecution for Journalists' Killings Amid Widespread Impunity
item.description: The International Federation of Journalists (IFJ) calls for governments to prosecute those responsible for killing journalists, warning of widespread impunity. Marking the International Day to End Impunity for Crimes Against Journalists, the IFJ highlighted ongoing threats and attacks faced by media workers globally.

item.title: CIS Youth Council Discusses New Cooperation Directions and Strategy
item.description: The 40th meeting of the CIS Youth Affairs Council, chaired by Kazakhstan, took place in Moscow. Representatives discussed youth policies and future joint work, approving programs for 2025-2026 and plans for 2027-2028. A new strategy for international youth cooperation for 2031-2040 was also discussed, emphasizing volunteerism and digital technologies.

item.title: Kazakh Tenge Weakened by 3% in October, National Bank Discloses Trading Volumes
item.description: The Kazakh Tenge depreciated by 3% in October, reaching 453.77 tenge per dollar. The National Bank did not conduct currency interventions. Average daily trading volume on the Kazakhstan Stock Exchange decreased to $397 million. The bank acquired $910 million from the National Fund to support government financing needs.

item.title: Kazakhstan Air Force Receives Second Airbus A400M Military Transport Aircraft
item.description: Kazakhstan's Air Defense Forces have received their second heavy military transport aircraft, an Airbus A400M Atlas, delivered from Spain to Almaty. The aircraft can be used for defense, disaster relief, evacuation, and humanitarian aid missions. Kazakh crews and technical personnel have been trained in Spain to operate the new aircraft.

item.title: Kazakhstan Nearing Completion of Engineering Surveys for Nuclear Power Plant
item.description: Kazakhstan is nearing completion of engineering and survey work for its first nuclear power plant project, "Balkhash." Intergovernmental agreements for the project were signed and ratified in May-June 2026, with an EPC contract signed in September 2026. Construction is planned to begin in 2027. A site for a second NPP, "Moyinkum," has been identified.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Grant Management of Technical Colleges to Entrepreneurs for 15 Years
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to involve private businesses more actively in managing technical colleges, with entrepreneurs set to take over 2-3 institutions per region for 15-year terms. This initiative aims to train at least 30,000 qualified specialists annually, meeting the demands of both domestic and international labor markets.

item.title: Regional Powers Concerned Over Potential US Retaliation Against Iran
item.description: Gulf states are reportedly worried about a potential US military strike against Iran, fearing they could become targets of Iranian retaliation. These concerns were a central theme at the Manama Dialogue security conference, where officials discussed the potential consequences of renewed conflict.

item.title: Construction of Balhash Nuclear Power Plant in Kazakhstan to Begin in 2027
item.description: Construction work on the Balhash Nuclear Power Plant in Kazakhstan is planned to commence in 2027. Engineering and survey work at the site are nearing completion. Intergovernmental agreements for the project were signed and ratified in May and June 2026, respectively.

item.title: Uzbekistan Enhances Labor Migration System and Citizen Training
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev chaired a meeting on improving labor migration, focusing on targeted language and professional training for citizens seeking overseas employment. The number of countries with organized labor migration agreements has grown to 27, and cooperation with employers has significantly expanded.

item.title: Kazakhstan Launches Checks on 11 Major Banks for Debt Load Calculations
item.description: Kazakhstan's Agency for Regulation and Development of the Financial Market is initiating a new oversight process, Debt Service Review (DSR), to check if 11 major banks correctly calculate borrowers' debt burden ratios. The aim is to prevent excessive lending and ensure responsible credit practices.

item.title: Kazakhstan Financial Regulator to Audit Borrower Debt Load Calculations at Major Banks
item.description: Kazakhstan's Financial Market Regulation and Development Agency will audit the debt load coefficient calculations for borrowers at 11 major banks. The initiative aims to ensure balanced borrower debt levels and promote responsible lending practices. A pilot project analyzing eight banks preceded this new oversight process.

item.title: At Least 22 Political Prisoners Held in Belarusian Psychiatric Hospitals, Rights Groups Report
item.description: At least 22 individuals recognized as political prisoners by Belarusian human rights advocates are reportedly undergoing forced treatment in psychiatric hospitals. This measure could lead to their indefinite detention outside the country's regular prison system. Accusations include insulting government officials and aiding extremist activities.

item.title: Iran Submits New Proposal to US on Opening Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Iran has presented a new proposal to the United States regarding the opening of the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran stated it is prepared to reopen the strait within two days if Washington fulfills its conditions. Previously, the Islamic Republic had proposed a one-week timeframe for this process.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Transport Sector Undergoes Modernization and Expansion
item.description: Uzbekistan is rapidly developing its modern transport infrastructure, including airports, high-speed trains, and metro networks. Reforms aim to enhance passenger services and national development. The aviation sector has seen a significant increase in airlines, aircraft, routes, flights, and passenger numbers.

item.title: Diverse Candidates Vie for Astana City Maslikhat Seats in Upcoming Elections
item.description: Astana's Akimat has published the list of registered candidates for the city Maslikhat elections on November 29. A total of 83 candidates are running in 17 single-mandate districts, with seven political parties fielding 101 candidates on party lists.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Increases Electricity Limit to 7 Kilowatts for Residential Buildings
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's National Electric Network (NESK) will raise the electricity consumption limit from 5 to 7 kilowatts, but only for multi-apartment buildings heated electrically. This aims to ensure adequate living conditions during winter, with 276 such buildings in Bishkek affected.

item.title: Uzbekistan Participates in Discussions on International Halal Economy Standards
item.description: Representatives from Uzbekistan's Agency for Technical Regulation attended the 21st General Assembly of the Standards and Metrology Institute for Islamic Countries (SMIIC) in Kazan. Discussions focused on developing the halal product market and enhancing international cooperation in standardization and certification.

item.title: Dushanbe to Implement AI-Powered Traffic Safety System for Schoolchildren
item.description: Dushanbe plans to introduce an AI-powered 'smart school zone' system to enhance student safety. The system will use surveillance cameras and smart traffic lights to monitor vehicle movement and alert children and school staff to potential dangers. The Ministry of Transport stated the project aims to prevent accidents near schools. Details on implementation timeline and cost are not yet available.

item.title: Kazakh Scientists Research Nuclear Reactor Safety Using Neutron Physics
item.description: Kazakh scientists are studying material properties and enhancing nuclear energy reliability through neutron physics methods. The safety and reliability of nuclear power depend not only on technological solutions but also on the quality and durability of materials under high temperature, pressure, and intense neutron radiation. The Institute of Nuclear Physics near Almaty, established in 1957, possesses the necessary experimental base for these studies, including the WWR-K research reactor.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Briefed on Karaganda Region's Economic Growth and Investment Projects
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev received an update on the socio-economic development of the Karaganda region, investment project implementation, and modernization plans. The region's economy grew 2.9% in nine months, with industrial production up 4.9%. Investment portfolio includes 186 projects by 2032, aiming to create 36,000 jobs.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Ninth-grader hospitalized in critical condition after teenage brawl
item.description: A ninth-grade student in Kazakhstan's Zhambyl region has been hospitalized in critical condition following a fight among teenagers. Police have opened a criminal case. Relatives allege the student was beaten for being late to a meeting with older students, citing bullying in local schools.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Karaganda region to implement 186 investment projects worth 7 trillion tenge
item.description: The Karaganda region in Kazakhstan is set to implement 186 investment projects totaling 7 trillion tenge by 2032, creating 36,000 jobs. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev was briefed on the region's socio-economic development, with a focus on industrial growth, raw material processing, and attracting investors.

item.title: Uzbekistan Interior Minister's Reception: 236 of 481 Appeals Resolved On-Site
item.description: During a reception led by the Minister of Internal Affairs, 236 out of 481 appeals from citizens and legal entities were resolved on the spot. The event aimed to strengthen trust between society and the state and facilitate dialogue. Appeals requiring further investigation have been placed under strict control.

item.title: 186 Projects Worth 7 Trillion Tenge Planned for Karaganda Region
item.description: The Karaganda region plans to implement 186 investment projects totaling 7 trillion tenge by 2032, creating 36,000 jobs. The region's economy grew 2.9% and industrial production 4.9% in the first nine months, with machine building up 26.2%. The region aims to attract investors and enhance infrastructure.

item.title: Kazakh Scientists Develop New Technology to Improve Asphalt Durability
item.description: Scientists at Kozybayev University have developed a new technology using industrial waste to enhance asphalt's resistance to water and high temperatures. The innovation aims to increase the strength and lifespan of asphalt concrete pavements. A pilot section of a road in the North Kazakhstan region has already tested the technology.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Named Among Press Freedom 'Predators'
item.description: Reporters Without Borders (RSF) has included Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev in its list of press freedom 'predators.' RSF cites his government's control over information through legislation, leading to increased restrictions, criminal prosecutions for 'false information,' and intimidation of independent journalists. The report highlights concerns about impunity for crimes against journalists.

item.title: Uzbekistan Reports 15% Reduction in Premature Mortality Due to Healthcare Reforms
item.description: Uzbekistan's healthcare reforms have led to a 15% decrease in premature mortality over five months, saving 855 lives, according to a report. The reforms focus on early disease detection, including a phased rollout of an early cancer detection program and initiatives for heart attack and stroke prevention. Next year, the program will expand nationwide.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Schoolboy Hospitalized After Peer Conflict in Zhambyl Region
item.description: A ninth-grader in Kazakhstan's Zhambyl region was hospitalized in intensive care following a conflict with peers. Relatives allege involvement of a local older student group, with tardiness to a meeting as a possible motive. Police have opened a criminal case and detained all involved.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Farmers to Access Subsidized Loans for Purebred Livestock
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has imported its first 300 purebred cattle, which have been sold out due to high demand. Farmers can now access subsidized loans at 3% annual interest to purchase livestock, aiming to improve meat production quality and develop the domestic livestock sector.

item.title: Tajikistan's Autumn Conscription Campaign Set to Begin
item.description: Tajikistan's autumn conscription campaign is scheduled to commence on October 1st and will continue until November 30th. The Ministry of Defense has provided answers to the most important questions regarding the military draft.

item.title: President Tokayev Awards State Honors to Qarmet Employees for Contributions
item.description: During a visit to Qarmet in Temirtau, President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev presented state awards to employees of the enterprise and related companies. Fifteen individuals were recognized for their significant contributions to Kazakhstan's industrial development.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Financial Market Agency Launches Checks on 11 Major Banks' Debt Load Calculations
item.description: Kazakhstan's Agency for Regulation and Development of the Financial Market (ARFR) has initiated regular checks on the accuracy of debt load ratio (DLR) calculations in 11 of the country's largest banks. The review aims to ensure responsible lending practices and prevent excessive client debt.

item.title: Kazakhstan Strengthens Control Over Bank Lending Practices
item.description: Kazakhstan's Agency for Regulation and Development of the Financial Market (ARDFM) is enhancing oversight of bank lending. The new Debt Service Review (DSR) process will assess how 11 banks calculate citizens' debt burden ratios to prevent household over-indebtedness. This aims to improve loan portfolio quality and ensure consistent lending rules.

item.title: Russian Region Restricts Migrant Work in Three More Sectors
item.description: Russia's Khanty-Mansi Autonomous Okrug will expand its list of professions closed to foreign citizens from January 1, 2027. Migrants will be barred from working in bakeries, warehouses, order pick-up points, and in culture and sports sectors. Authorities cite a desire to prioritize local employment, though specialists in oil, gas, and construction remain needed.

item.title: Candidates Announced for Almaty City Maslikhat Elections on November 29
item.description: A list of registered candidates for the Almaty City Maslikhat elections, scheduled for November 29, has been published. A total of 111 candidates were nominated across 21 single-mandate districts. After withdrawals and rejections, the final candidate list is now available for voters to consider.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Continue Developing Cooperation with All States, Says President
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated Kazakhstan's commitment to inter-ethnic and inter-religious harmony and the principle of "Unity in Diversity." He emphasized the need for internal peace and stability to continue reforms, vowing to hold accountable those who harm the country. Kazakhstan will strengthen cooperation with all nations.

item.title: President Mirziyoyev Visits 'Intil' Center for Employment Abroad Training
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited the 'Intil' International Language and Vocational Training Center in Tashkent. The center helps citizens prepare for employment abroad, offering language courses, vocational training, and document processing. The President emphasized training skilled specialists, not just laborers, for foreign work.

item.title: Afghan Students Recount Hope and Disbelief During Taliban Takeover
item.description: University students in Afghanistan describe their journey from hope to shock as provincial capitals fell to the Taliban. Despite approaching graduation, they believed security forces would prevail, never imagining the rapid collapse that led to widespread darkness and surrender orders.

item.title: 22 Gas Filling Stations in Nukus Fined for Simultaneous Price Increases
item.description: Twenty-two gas filling stations in Nukus, Karakalpakstan, have been fined for colluding to raise compressed gas prices. The Committee for the Development of Competition investigated after a citizen complaint, finding prices increased by an average of 1050 UZS per cubic meter. Nine stations appealed the decision in court.
